questions.stem: The phenomenon by which molecules of a gas or liquid are held on the surface of a solid is called:

options.option_text: Absorption
Adsorption
Desorption
Chemisorption

questions.explanation: Adsorption is the accumulation of molecules (adsorbate) on the surface of a solid (adsorbent), not throughout its bulk. Absorption occurs throughout the bulk. Chemisorption is a type of adsorption involving chemical bonds.

questions.stem: Which property of colloidal solutions causes a beam of light passing through them to become visible due to scattering?

options.option_text: Brownian motion
Electrophoresis
Tyndall effect
Coagulation

questions.explanation: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles (1–1000 nm), making the beam path visible. True solutions (particles < 1 nm) do not show this. Tyndall first described it in 1869.

questions.stem: A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction without being consumed. How does it achieve this?

options.option_text: By increasing the temperature of the reaction mixture significantly
By raising the activation energy so reactants collide more forcefully
By permanently bonding to reactants and forming new intermediates
By providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy

questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternate reaction mechanism with a lower activation energy (Ea). More molecules then have sufficient energy to react, increasing the rate. The catalyst is regenerated at the end and so is not consumed overall.

questions.stem: The random, zigzag motion of colloidal particles caused by unequal bombardment by the molecules of the dispersion medium is called:

options.option_text: Brownian motion
Tyndall scattering
Electrophoresis
Peptisation (alternative interpretation)

questions.explanation: Brownian motion (named after Robert Brown, 1827) is the random thermal motion of colloidal particles. Unequal bombardment by dispersion-medium molecules from different sides causes the zigzag path. It helps keep colloids from settling.

questions.stem: In heterogeneous catalysis, the catalytic action occurs at the surface of the solid catalyst. Which step in this process involves the reactant molecules sticking to the catalyst surface?

options.option_text: Desorption of products from the catalyst surface
Diffusion of products away from the catalyst surface
Adsorption of reactants on the catalyst surface
Activation of the catalyst by heating it above threshold

questions.explanation: In heterogeneous catalysis, the sequence is: (1) adsorption of reactants on catalyst surface, (2) chemical reaction at the surface, (3) desorption of products, (4) diffusion of products away. Adsorption is the first and rate-determining step.

questions.stem: Colloidal gold particles are used in the treatment of certain diseases. These particles carry negative charge. When an electric field is applied, the particles will migrate towards:

options.option_text: The negative electrode (cathode) as like charges attract
The positive electrode (anode) due to opposite charge attraction
No movement occurs as colloidal particles are electrically neutral
Both electrodes simultaneously due to alternating charge induction

questions.explanation: Electrophoresis is the migration of charged colloidal particles under an electric field. Negatively charged particles migrate towards the positive electrode (anode), following opposite-charge attraction. Colloidal gold (as used by Faraday) carries negative charge and moves to the anode.

questions.stem: The Freundlich adsorption isotherm relates the extent of adsorption (x/m) to pressure (P) at constant temperature as x/m = kP^(1/n). Which condition does this isotherm fail to satisfy at high pressures?

options.option_text: It predicts x/m falls to zero at high pressure, contradicting experimental data
It ignores temperature variation but works perfectly at high-pressure conditions
It assumes multilayer adsorption while experiments show only monolayer formation
It predicts x/m rises indefinitely, but adsorption must saturate at monolayer coverage

questions.explanation: The Freundlich isotherm (x/m = kP^(1/n), n > 1) predicts that adsorption increases without limit as pressure rises. In reality, once the solid surface is fully covered (monolayer saturation), adsorption cannot increase further. The Langmuir isotherm corrects this by assuming a fixed number of equivalent surface sites.
